2026 SEMA Show • Mitsubishi Returns to Las Vegas With the Fresh 2028 Outlander Diamond Trail Edition
The DM Vans LV7 Backcountry Is a Spacious Camper Van That Makes Everyday Routines More Comfortable
20 photos
Photo: DM Vans
Some people argue that van life is losing its appeal, with many travelers moving away from life on the road and returning to traditional homes. But a quick search on social media under the van life hashtag suggests otherwise. The van life trend is still going strong, and interest in camper vans continues to inspire new builds.
If anything, more van conversion companies are emerging to meet the increasing demand, offering well-equipped rigs for everything from weekend escapes to full-time van living. One of the latest manufacturers to catch my attention is DM Vans, a boutique Colorado-based shop that has been building custom camper vans based on the RAM ProMaster chassis since 2018.
The company was founded by two experienced van lifers who wanted to help others fulfill their travel dreams, and they use their firsthand knowledge of life on the road to create practical roving homes . They call their rigs “Class B Lifestyle Vehicles” and have completed over 800 custom builds so far.
Their offering includes three models - the LV3 aimed at weekend warriors or solo travelers, the LV5 for couples seeking more than a camper, and the LV7 designed for extended trips or full-time use. Each is manufactured to RVIA standards, with high-quality materials, excellent craftsmanship, and great attention to detail.
Photo: DM Vans Built on the RAM ProMaster 159-inch Extended SLT chassis, the 2027 LV7 Backcountry is the company’s most capable and complete conversion aimed at people who are serious about van living . It combines a reliable platform with a spacious interior designed to deliver an upgraded mobile living experience, plus an electrical system that enables extended off-grid adventures.
With maximum cargo volume, generous headroom, and a square interior geometry, the RAM ProMaster provides a great base for this conversion. Not to mention, it comes with a range of handy driver-assistance features, including Full-Speed Forward-Collision Warning, Blind-Spot and Cross-Path Detection, and Active Driving Assist.
Finished in dark granite gray, the van conversion featured in the photos and the video below is a rather unassuming build, with very few details that point to its camper identity. The most obvious one is the full-length roof rack, which has become standard equipment for the 2027 model year.
Photo: DM Vans DM Vans added this feature to give owners extra space for carrying gear and the possibility to configure the top of the van as they please with fewer holes in the roof. The rack is compatible with most awnings on the market, and an optional side ladder attaches directly to it for easier roof access.
For LV7 Backcountry’s interior, the outfitter focused on space efficiency. They used the 463 cubic feet of living space to include a full kitchen, a comfortable raised bed, seating and dining space, and smart storage designed for extended living. At the front, they kept the floor plan open, with no divider wall behind the driver’s and passenger’s seats, which are also swivel seats, so they become part of the living space at camp.
Style-wise, DM Vans went for a modern, minimalist design with a bright Scandinavian-inspired aesthetic. White cabinetry with flat, handleless cabinet faces and flush-mounted drawers gives the interior a clean look, while natural wood countertops and a stained tongue-and-groove ceiling add a bit of warmth and texture.
The white-dominated color scheme might not be to everyone’s taste, but it definitely helps make the interior feel open and uncluttered.
Photo: DM Vans The kitchen runs along the driver’s side of the van and is equipped with an induction cooktop, a sink, and a 12-volt compressor fridge. Instead of the typical backsplash, the LV7 features a nifty wooden shelf that is perfect for keeping utensils or spices easily accessible. An opening window above the counter is another nice touch, allowing for nice views and improved ventilation while cooking.
A seating arrangement is included nearby, with a long bench along the passenger side and a smaller one next to the kitchenette. Apart from seating, these upholstered benches double as storage and as steps leading to the elevated rear bed. A versatile Lagun table slides out from under the bed. You can position it however you like to use it for dining or working, and when you don’t need it anymore, it neatly stows away, opening up the floor space. A Trelino composting toilet is stored inside the smaller cube.
For the sleeping arrangements, buyers can choose between a short king bed or a full-size bed with a full-height wardrobe beside it, as shown in the video. The wardrobe is a really nice addition for those living in their vans full-time, as it offers ample storage for clothes and personal belongings. The storage options in this conversion also include upper cabinets, an open bungee shelf, a multi-functional storage unit above the bed, and rear door organizers.
Photo: DM Vans But the largest storage compartment is the open garage area under the bed. Built-in side cabinets hold the van’s systems, while the central area is perfect for larger items or bulky equipment. What’s more, the floor of this garage is carpeted, so it doesn’t look too utilitarian.
But one of LV7 Backcountry’s strongest suits is its electrical system, which is perfectly capable of handling long off-grid journeys. It includes a 1,200Ah lithium battery bank (four 300Ah batteries) with a stated capacity of 14.4 kWh, two 200-watt solar panels, dual 50-amp DC-to-DC chargers with MPPT solar controllers, and a 3,000-watt inverter.
The water system, on the other hand, is not so impressive, as the van only carries 7 gallons (26 liters) of fresh water and 7 gallons of gray. The good part, though, is that the tanks are easy to replenish and the sink has an accumulator that allows you to control the water flow.
The van is also equipped with a Peak Heating System and reversible front and rear ventilation fans, plus a high-efficiency 12-volt AC unit, giving you multiple ways to manage airflow and interior temperature.
Photo: DM Vans DM Vans offers a list of optional upgrades as well, including an L-track system for the garage area, additional Lagun tables, reflective interior window covers, running boards, a spare tire carrier, all-terrain tires, and traction boards. Bug nets and an external Starlink port are also available, and buyers can also extend their off-grid setup with more solar and battery capacity.
The 2027 DM Vans LV7 Backcountry camper van is now available for pre-order, with a starting price of $124,800. Deliveries are scheduled to begin in early November.
